frequency_question: How often does a recipient nation successfully stand up domestic manufacturing for advanced long-range precision guided munitions within 24 months of receiving them under wartime conditions?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign states receiving complex foreign cruise or ballistic missile technology while actively engaged in a major conventional war; excludes peacetime co-production, simple ammunition manufacturing, or non-state actors.

cases.name: South Korea / US surface-to-air missile co-production (1970s)
Iran / various foreign missile reverse-engineering under wartime conditions (1980-1988)
Ukraine / domestic missile initiatives post-2014 conflict initiation

coverage_note: 4 named historical comparable cases; believed exhaustive for major wartime advanced missile tech transfers.
known_gaps: Historical data for clandestine wartime transfers is sparse; reliance on open-source military technology history.
skeleton: Enumerate major wartime complex weapons transfers since 1950 resulting in successful domestic serial production lines within two years.
multiplier: 4 observed historical analog instances with 1 hit.
validity_reason: Based on long-term historical state defense industrial capabilities and wartime friction, which evolves slowly over decades.
